incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: latency.p99.redwood-api.prod.east-1 > 9.5s (alert at 2026-03-14T10:12:08Z)

pagerduty: PagerDuty incident INC-20260314-0812 created and routed to on-call (sanjay).

sanjay: acked the page :white_check_mark: taking lead. I'm jumping in — gathering context.

mia: seeing the same in Grafana, p95 ~ 1.2s but p99 spiking to 10-12s across text-generation routes. Not universal — east-1 is hot.

lucy: Any deploys around that time? CI looks clean, but I see a spike in KV cache miss rate for model-alfred-v2.

eng-sre-bot: Autoscaler logs: scale_event at 2026-03-14T10:08:22Z -> requested +40 GPUs, provisioned +2, throttled by quota.

sanjay: OK that explains tail latency. If autoscaler couldn't get capacity, request backlog grew and batching hit slow hosts. Initiating mitigation.

mia: quick mitigation checklist: 1) route traffic away from east-1 2) enable fallback smaller model 3) reduce max_batch_size 4) enable aggressive prefix caching. Which do we want first?

lucy: I'll kick traffic failover to eu-west as a short-term measure. Doing: `infra route set --from east-1 --to eu-west --weight 0.6 --reason "latency p99"`

eng-sre-bot: Command accepted, traffic policy update queued. Estimated propagation 45s.

sanjay: While that rolls, Mia — can you flip fallback to model-alfred-v2-quant? It's cheaper and lower mem. Use the canary route to avoid regressions.

mia: running rollout: `redwood rollout create --service inference --route canary --model model-alfred-v2-quant --max-traffic 0.3`

lucy: routing change at 10:13:12Z shows initial drop in requests to east-1. p99 down a bit to ~7s, p95 unchanged.

sanjay: Good. Also reducing max_batch_size on east-1 to 8 to avoid massive queuing on slow nodes. Applying config: `cfg apply --service inference --region east-1 --max_batch_size 8`

eng-sre-bot: Config applied. Note: persistent KV cache miss surge persists (miss rate 78%).

mia: Increasing KV cache warmup target: `kvcache prewarm --model model-alfred-v2 --region east-1 --prefixes recent-1h` — starting now.

lucy: Prewarm started; observing slow but steady KV hit-rate improvement. p99 trending to 4.3s after 2 mins.

sanjay: Good. I'll call for temporary quota bump with infra: `@next-oncall can you escalate GPU quota request for east-1? We need short-term capacity to drain backlog.`

next-oncall: On it — filing ticket with cloud provider now, pinging account manager. ETA optimistic 20-30m.

mia: Customer impact check: only a small subset of heavy generation endpoints show degraded throughput. No major 5xx spike, mostly elevated request latency. Notifying support to update status page with limited performance degradation in US-East.

lucy: Support updated status page: "Limited performance degradation for text generation in US-East; mitigation in progress."

sanjay: After the routing + fallback + batch cap + kvcache prewarm, p99 stabilized near 3.8s. Still above SLO (2.0s) but much improved. Moving to recovery phase and timeline.

mia: Suggested follow-ups: - post-incident: examine autoscaler backoff behavior and quota prefetching - add a runbook step to fail traffic to regional spare pool when provisioned capacity < 20% - tune kvcache eviction for heavy tail loads

eng-sre-bot: Incident INC-20260314-0812 -> status: mitigated, summary: regional autoscaler quota exhaustion caused high p99 tail; mitigations implemented: partial failover, model fallback, batch cap, kvcache prewarm.

sanjay: Handoff to next-oncall for monitoring and postmortem. Next-oncall please own follow-up tasks and timeline.

next-oncall: Acking handoff :handshake: I'll consolidate notes and open a postmortem doc. Tentative blameless postmortem within 48h.

mia: Thanks all. If anything regresses, re-page. Closing Slack thread but keeping PD incident open until postmortem created. :pray:
